description: Explicit mapping between cell_state database columns and fire behavior fuel model concepts. Use this to translate sensor readings into fuel model reasoning inputs.

fuel_moisture.reasoning_guidance: Map to dead fuel moisture scenarios D1-D4. Values below 6% approach D1 (Very Low). Values 6-9% map to D2 (Low). Values 9-12% map to D3 (Moderate). Values above 12% map to D4 (High). For dynamic fuel models, also estimate live herbaceous moisture using the herbaceous_curing_table if curing level is observable.

vegtation_greeness_ndvi.document_concept: Live herbaceous moisture content / degree of curing
vegtation_greeness_ndvi.reasoning_guidance: NDVI is a proxy for vegetation greenness and live fuel moisture. High NDVI (approaching 1.0) suggests uncured, green vegetation with live herbaceous moisture >= 120%. Low NDVI (approaching 0) suggests cured or absent vegetation with live herbaceous moisture <= 30%. Use as a continuous signal to interpolate live moisture scenario L1-L4 and to determine whether dynamic fuel models will transfer herbaceous load to dead.

vegetaion_cover_evc.reasoning_guidance: Existing Vegetation Cover (EVC) informs the dominant fuel type. Dense shrub cover suggests SH fuel types. Mixed grass-shrub cover suggests GS. Open grassland suggests GR. Forest with understory suggests TU or TL. Use in combination with wind_speed, fuel_moisture, and region to select the appropriate fuel type category (NB, GR, GS, SH, TU, TL, SB).

temperature_c.document_concept: Indirect influence on fuel moisture drying rate
temperature_c.reasoning_guidance: Not a direct fuel model input. High temperatures accelerate fuel drying, pushing dead fuel moisture toward lower scenarios (D1/D2). Use as a contextual signal when fuel_moisture reading is absent or uncertain.

humidity_pct.document_concept: Indirect influence on dead fuel moisture equilibrium
humidity_pct.reasoning_guidance: Not a direct fuel model input. Low relative humidity (< 20%) is associated with D1/D2 dead fuel moisture scenarios and elevated fire risk. High humidity (> 60%) is associated with D3/D4 scenarios and suppressed spread.

wind_speed_mps.reasoning_guidance: Direct fire behavior driver. Fire behavior charts in the document use midflame wind speed in mi/h. Convert: 1 m/s = 2.237 mi/h. Standard comparison charts run from 0 to 20 mi/h. Wind speed is the primary driver of rate of spread increase across all fuel types.

wind_direction_deg.reasoning_guidance: Used to determine headfire direction relative to fuel layout. Not a fuel model parameter per se, but critical for operational fire spread prediction. Combined with slope aspect, determines upslope/wind alignment scenarios.
wind_direction_deg.wind_direction_interpretation: Wind direction is meteorological (wind comes from the stated bearing, clockwise from North). Fire spreads opposite: bearing + 180° mod 360°. Western longitudes are negative — "more west" means more negative. Example: 90° reading at POINT(-118.541837, 34.286735) → wind from East → fire spreads West → toward lower (more negative) longitudes

fire_intensity.document_concept: Observed or modeled flame length / fireline intensity
fire_intensity.reasoning_guidance: If fire_intensity > 0, the cell is actively burning or recently burned. Use adjective class thresholds to classify intensity level. A cell with fire_intensity in flame length equivalent > 25 ft maps to Extreme class.

risk_score.document_concept: Composite fire behavior risk assessment output
risk_score.reasoning_guidance: Derived field — should reflect combination of fuel type, dead fuel moisture scenario, live moisture scenario, and wind speed. Use fuel model parameters and adjective class thresholds to validate or compute.

region.reasoning_guidance: Informs extinction moisture selection. Arid/semiarid regions default to 15% extinction moisture (dry climate models). Subhumid to humid regions use 30-40% extinction moisture. Region combined with vegetaion_cover_evc and fuel_moisture narrows fuel type selection.

grid_row_grid_column_layer.reasoning_guidance: Layer may indicate surface (0) vs. elevated fuel strata. The document addresses surface fire behavior only — crown fire initiation is a separate model. Layer 0 is the relevant layer for Rothermel surface fire spread model inputs.
